messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways, 35 mph on city streets.
• “No‑limit” roads exist in some rural counties. | Exceeding posted limits can lead to fines, points, and possible license suspension. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• The “Texas Safe Seat” law requires proper installation. | Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine and 1 point. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | Violations carry a $50 fine and 1 point. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• For commercial drivers, the limit is 0.04%.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas has a “zero‑tolerance” law for drivers under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• “Right‑of‑way” rules apply at intersections, roundabouts, and when merging. | Failure to yield can lead to points and fines. | | **School Bus** | • Stop for a school bus with its stop sign extended and lights flashing.
• Vehicles must stop on both sides of the road. | Violations can result in a $200 fine and 2 points. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other vehicles.
• “Lane‑change” violations can lead to points. | | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is a $200 fine. | | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Must display registration stickers.
• Proof of insurance is required.
• Failure to register or insure can lead to fines and vehicle impoundment. | | | **Points System** | • Accumulating 4 points in 2 years can lead to license suspension.
• Points vary by offense (e.g., 1 point for speeding, 2 for DUI). | | | **Traffic School** | • Eligible drivers can attend a state‑approved traffic school to reduce points. | Must be completed within 12 months of the offense. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Trucks, buses, and motorcycles have specific regulations (e.g., lane usage, horn use). | | ### How to Find Specific Laws - **Texas Transportation Code**: The primary source for all traffic laws. - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)**: Offers guides, FAQs, and downloadable handbooks. - **Texas Legislature Online**: Search for statutes by keyword or bill number. - **Local County Ordinances**: Some counties have additional regulations (e.g., speed limits, parking restrictions). ### Quick Resources - **Texas DPS Traffic Law Handbook** – PDF available on the DPS website. - **Texas.gov** – Official state portal with links to traffic regulations. - **Texas A&M Transportation Institute** – Research and updates on traffic safety. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to handle a particular situation!
